_note: Collective scope: the population a record relates to, kept apart from Native entity identity. A scope is never a Cedar entity, never carries a CE-XXXXX-CC uid, never stands in for a failed entity match and never receives dollars. Owner's decision of 2026-09-05 (docs/COLLECTIVE_SCOPE_DECISION_2026-09-05.md). This file is the whole vocabulary: a scope code the writer meets that is not here stops the dataset. Versioned: a membership result is reproducible only against the version and the register release it was computed with.

element.scope: A code from `scopes` below; a parameterised scope carries its parameter after a colon (federally-recognized-tribes-in-state:OK).
element.relationship: How the record relates to the population: one of `relationships`.
element.as_of: The date the population is defined at, YYYY-MM-DD, or null when the source does not fix one.
element.basis: The source words, or the source field, the scope was read from. Never blank.

null_vs_empty: null: the record was not evaluated for collective scope (the terminal has not read its source for a population). []: evaluated, and the record names no collective population.

relationships.addressed: The source directs a communication or an opportunity to this population: an invitation to consult, a call for comment. An invitation is not participation.
relationships.applies_to: The source establishes applicability to this population: a statute's or a rule's applicability clause.
relationships.eligible_class: Members of the population may qualify, subject to the criteria the source states. Eligibility is not receipt.
relationships.aggregate_population: A statistic or an amount describes this population collectively. It is never a share per member.
relationships.general_subject: The source discusses this population without establishing applicability to any member.

as_of_rules.source_defined: The source names the date its population is defined at (a statute freezing membership to entities recognized on a stated date; a program's application deadline).
as_of_rules.record_date: The record's own date, where the source type addresses the population as it stood then (an invitation).
as_of_rules.publication_date: The publication date, a documented fallback for source types the guide names; never a substitute for a source-defined date.
as_of_rules.unknown: No date can be established from the source; membership at any date is unknown.

membership_kinds.register_class: Membership is the register's class of an entity: evaluable per entity for the classes listed. A national count is not displayed until the class populations are reconciled against the official list, and no count is stored here.
membership_kinds.undetermined: Membership cannot be evaluated from the register: the source's own definition decides, and the record keeps the stated scope with individual membership unknown.
membership_kinds.none: The scope is a subject, not a population with members: nothing expands to it.

federally-recognized-tribes.name: Federally recognized tribes
federally-recognized-tribes.definition: The tribal governments on the Secretary of the Interior's list published under 25 U.S.C. 5131, including the Alaska Native village governments, as the list stood at `as_of`.

membership.reconciliation: Owed on the terminal: a uid-level reconciliation of the register's two classes against the BIA list in the Federal Register notice of 2026-01-30 (aliases, constituent bodies, unresolved differences), before any national count is shown. The proposal's 577 was the register's class totals, not the list.

federally-recognized-tribes-in-state.name: Federally recognized tribes in a state
federally-recognized-tribes-in-state.definition: The federally recognized tribes a source relates to a state: headquartered there, holding land there, served by an office there, or as the source defines. The source's predicate is recorded in `basis`.

membership.why: Headquarters, trust land and service area are different predicates; the register's state field is the headquarters state, which is not automatically what a source means. Individual membership stays unknown until the predicate is explicit and the evidence exists.

alaska-native-villages.name: Alaska Native village governments
alaska-native-villages.definition: The federally recognized Alaska Native village governments, as the list stood at `as_of`.

alaska-native-corporations.name: Alaska Native Corporations
alaska-native-corporations.definition: The regional, village and group corporations organised under ANCSA. Not federally recognized tribes; a source that uses the ISDA definition of Indian tribe (Yellen v. Confederated Tribes of the Chehalis Reservation, 2021) reaches them where the recognized-tribe list does not, and the two scopes are recorded separately.

native-hawaiian-organizations.name: Native Hawaiian Organizations
native-hawaiian-organizations.definition: Organizations a source treats as Native Hawaiian Organizations under the definition it names (SBA's, a statute's, a program's own). The definition is recorded in `basis`.

membership.why: Definitions differ in organisation, control and beneficiary requirements; the register's class is not a program's definition.

indian-country.name: Indian Country, general
indian-country.definition: The record concerns Indian Country without a defined population. General relevance only.
